issues.estimate_rationale: This establishes the core service contract, persistence model, and integration boundary used by every delivery channel.

issues.description: Implement email delivery through the unified service, including provider integration, message formatting, provider response capture, and delivery-state updates. Preserve the existing email use cases while routing them through the new service interface.

issues.description: Add admin dashboard views and filters for notification status, channel, recipient, timestamps, retry attempts, and failure reasons. Use the unified service’s delivery records to support investigation without requiring access to individual provider systems.

issues.description: Map and migrate notification preferences from the three existing tables into the canonical preference model. Make the backfill idempotent, produce reconciliation metrics, and define handling for conflicting or incomplete legacy records.

issues.title: Cut over notification producers to the unified service
issues.description: Update existing notification producers to use the unified service, run validation and parity checks against legacy behavior, and disable the old notification paths after successful rollout. issues.estimate_rationale: The cutover spans multiple existing producers, production rollout coordination, parity validation, and legacy-system retirement.

single.epic_title: Protect Public API Capacity with Client Limits and Quotas

issues.title: Define public API traffic-control policies
issues.description: Specify the rate-limit algorithms, endpoint throttling rules, per-API-key monthly quota semantics, reset timing, response codes, headers, and behavior for requests without a recognized API key. Produce an implementation-ready policy that can be applied consistently across public endpoints.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work is primarily policy definition but requires agreement on several interacting enforcement and client-facing behaviors.

issues.title: Add client request rate limiting
issues.description: Implement shared rate limiting for public API clients using the approved policy, with configurable limits and a consistent 429 response when a client exceeds its allowance. Include standard limit and retry information in responses and ensure the limiter works correctly across multiple API instances.
issues.estimate_rationale: The implementation requires distributed state, middleware integration, configuration, and reliable behavior across horizontally scaled API instances.

issues.title: Throttle high-impact public endpoints
issues.description: Apply endpoint-specific throttling to public endpoints whose traffic can consume disproportionate resources, such as expensive or high-contention operations. Throttling must isolate noisy integrations from other clients and produce predictable responses or delays without blocking unrelated endpoint traffic.
issues.estimate_rationale: Endpoint classification, resource isolation, and integration with existing request handling make this broader than a single generic middleware change.

issues.title: Enforce monthly API-key request quotas
issues.description: Track requests by API key, enforce each key’s configured monthly quota, and automatically reset usage at the defined monthly boundary. Return a distinct quota-exhausted response with remaining quota and reset information, while preventing race conditions that could allow significant overuse.
issues.estimate_rationale: Accurate distributed usage accounting, reset handling, concurrency control, and client-visible quota state are required.

issues.title: Add traffic-control monitoring and API documentation
issues.description: Add metrics and dashboards or alerts for rate-limit rejections, endpoint throttling, quota exhaustion, and unusual concentration by API key. Document all controls, response headers, status codes, configuration expectations, and recommended client retry behavior for public API consumers.
issues.estimate_rationale: This combines observable operational signals with externally visible documentation that must accurately describe all enforcement paths.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: The plan covers all the aspects mentioned in the proposal: rate limiting, throttling, quotas, and documentation. It also includes monitoring which adds a valuable operational aspect.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Each task is distinct and necessary, with clear dependencies that logically flow from one to the next without unnecessary overlap or padding.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: The dependencies are well-defined, ensuring a logical sequence of implementation. For example, defining policies (task 1) is a prerequisite for all subsequent tasks.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: The estimates seem proportionate to the work described. The larger point values are assigned to more complex tasks such as implementing rate limiting and throttling, while less complex tasks like documentation (task 5) have a lower point value.

multiagent.epic_title: Protect Public API Capacity with Fair Usage Controls

issues.title: Define public API usage policies
issues.description: Document the public endpoints in scope, client identity rules, default rate limits, throttling behavior, per-key monthly quotas, reset timing, and expected error or response headers. Produce configuration requirements that implementation issues can use without making policy decisions during development.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main effort is aligning endpoint scope, client identity, limits, and reset semantics across stakeholders.

issues.title: Build shared client usage enforcement primitives
issues.description: Implement the shared mechanisms for identifying clients by API key, maintaining atomic request counters, applying configurable policies, and returning enforcement decisions. The primitives must support distributed API instances and avoid allowing concurrent requests to bypass limits.
issues.estimate_rationale: Distributed counters, concurrency correctness, and integration with existing request handling create the primary technical complexity.

issues.title: Enforce per-client API rate limits
issues.description: Apply the shared enforcement primitives to public API requests so clients exceeding their configured request rate receive a consistent rate-limit response. Include standard limit and retry metadata and ensure normal requests remain unaffected while under the limit.
issues.estimate_rationale: This requires integrating policy-driven request rejection across public endpoints and validating client-facing response behavior.

issues.title: Add fair throttling to public endpoints
issues.description: Add endpoint-level throttling that limits the impact of noisy integrations through configurable concurrency or traffic-shaping controls rather than relying only on rejected requests. Preserve service responsiveness for other clients and define the behavior returned when an endpoint cannot accept more work.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work spans endpoint integration and capacity-sensitive behavior, with tuning needs depending on existing request processing patterns.

issues.title: Track and enforce monthly API-key quotas
issues.description: Record usage per API key, enforce each key’s configured monthly quota, and reset usage at the defined monthly boundary without losing isolation between keys. Expose remaining quota, reset timing, and a consistent response when a key has exhausted its allowance.
issues.estimate_rationale: Persistent usage accounting, boundary-safe monthly resets, and quota enforcement add more state and failure-mode complexity than rolling rate limits.

issues.title: Add usage-control monitoring and documentation
issues.description: Create dashboards, metrics, and alerts for rate-limit rejections, throttled requests, quota exhaustion, and enforcement-store failures. Document the limits, response metadata, reset behavior, and integration guidance for public API consumers.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope includes both operational instrumentation across enforcement paths and externally usable API documentation.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: scores a 4 because it covers all aspects of the proposal with specific tasks that address rate limiting, throttling, and quotas. It also includes a task to document policies and create monitoring, which is not explicitly required but adds value.

rows.challenge: Coverage: 'every table that holds personal data' implies discovery/audit work that a plan focused on the download button will skip entirely.

issues.title: Inventory personal-data sources
issues.description: Identify every database table, relationship, and file or object-storage location that contains personal data associated with an account. Document the fields and identifiers required for inclusion in the export, including any sensitive data that requires special handling.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope depends on discovering and classifying data across the existing schema and storage integrations.

issues.title: Design the portable export format
issues.description: Define the archive structure, file formats, naming conventions, metadata, and serialization rules for exporting the sources identified in the inventory. Ensure the format is machine-readable and clearly maps records back to their originating data source.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work is bounded but requires decisions that affect every exported data source and downstream implementation.

issues.title: Build complete personal-data export generation
issues.description: Implement a backend export workflow that gathers the account’s personal data from every inventoried source and packages it into one archive using the approved portable format. Handle large datasets, partial failures, repeat requests, and cleanup of temporary export artifacts without exposing another user’s data.
issues.estimate_rationale: This spans multiple data sources, archive creation, failure handling, and potentially resource-intensive processing.

issues.title: Secure export access and retention
issues.description: Add authorization checks so users can request and download only their own exports, and define secure storage, expiration, deletion, and audit behavior for generated archives. Protect export endpoints and temporary files against unauthorized access and predictable-download attacks.
issues.estimate_rationale: Security controls must cover request authorization, artifact access, retention, and auditability across the export lifecycle.

issues.title: Add export controls to Account Settings
issues.description: Add an Account Settings experience that lets a user request an export, see whether it is processing or ready, download the resulting archive, and understand failures or expiration. Prevent duplicate accidental submissions while allowing a new request when appropriate.
issues.estimate_rationale: The UI requires request state management, download handling, and clear privacy-oriented user messaging.

issues.title: Verify export completeness and isolation
issues.description: Create automated and integration tests that seed personal data across every inventoried source, generate an archive, and verify that all expected records are present in the documented format. Test authorization, cross-account isolation, expiration, retries, large exports, and failure cleanup.
issues.estimate_rationale: Coverage must span all data sources plus security, lifecycle, and scale scenarios, with ongoing protection against omissions.

issues.title: Document export contents and limitations
issues.description: Publish internal and user-facing documentation describing what the archive contains, its format, availability period, and how users can request it. Keep the data-source inventory and export documentation maintainable as new personal-data sources are added.
issues.estimate_rationale: Documentation is bounded but must align with the complete source inventory and the implemented archive contract.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: Broad coverage of all necessary tasks; clear dependencies ensure a logical flow from inventory to implementation to testing. Each goal is addressed with specific tasks or stories.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: No redundant issues identified; each task addresses unique aspects of the project without unnecessary overlap. The plan avoids padding and focuses on essential elements.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies are logically structured, ensuring that foundational tasks (inventory, format design) precede more complex implementation and testing phases. This prevents premature work and ensures a coherent development process.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: Estimates appear proportional to the described work, with larger points assigned to more complex tasks like building the export generation and verifying completeness. The inventory task is appropriately sized given its critical importance as a foundation for all subsequent steps.

issues.title: Inventory personal-data sources
issues.description: Identify every database table and related storage location that contains personal data associated with a user account, including ownership and export transformations. Produce an auditable mapping that the export implementation and future schema changes can use to verify coverage.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main effort is tracing personal data across schemas and related storage, with legal and privacy review unknowns.

issues.title: Build complete personal-data archive generation
issues.description: Implement a backend export workflow that gathers the data sources defined in the inventory, packages the results into one downloadable archive, and handles large exports without request timeouts. Include clear export status, failure handling, and a retention or expiration policy for generated archives.
issues.estimate_rationale: This spans all identified data sources, archive generation, asynchronous processing, storage, expiration, and failure handling.

issues.title: Secure export authorization and delivery
issues.description: Enforce that export requests and downloads are limited to the authenticated account owner, with appropriate authorization checks, secure archive storage, protected download access, and safeguards against exposing another user’s data. Record the security-relevant export events needed for investigation and compliance.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work involves authorization, protected archive delivery, retention controls, and security-event integration.

issues.title: Add export controls to Account Settings
issues.description: Add a user-facing control in Account Settings to request a data export, show whether generation is pending or complete, and provide the download action when the archive is ready. Explain archive expiration and display actionable errors without exposing sensitive data.
issues.estimate_rationale: The UI requires request, status, and download states plus integration with the asynchronous export API.

issues.title: Verify export completeness and privacy protections
issues.description: Add automated and reviewable test coverage that validates every inventoried personal-data source appears in the archive, archive generation handles representative large and failing datasets, and unauthorized users cannot request or download another account’s export. Include regression checks for archive expiration and sensitive-data leakage in errors or logs.
issues.estimate_rationale: Coverage must span data completeness, asynchronous failures, authorization boundaries, expiration, and leakage checks across the export workflow.

issues.title: Document export coverage and operations
issues.description: Document the supported personal-data sources, archive format, retention period, operational monitoring, failure recovery, and procedure for updating the inventory when new personal-data storage is introduced. Provide material suitable for engineering operations and legal or compliance review.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope is bounded documentation and operational guidance based on the implemented export behavior.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: The plan covers all aspects of the original proposal, including identifying data sources, creating a secure export mechanism, user interface integration, verification of completeness and privacy, and documentation. It demonstrates thorough planning with clear dependencies between tasks.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: The plan is concise, avoiding unnecessary or redundant issues. Each issue addresses a distinct aspect of the implementation, ensuring that all necessary components are covered without overlap.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies are logically set up, with foundational tasks (inventory and build) preceding dependent ones (security, user interface, verification). This structure ensures a coherent workflow and minimizes potential integration issues.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: Estimates appear proportionate to the work described. The inventory task is appropriately lightweight given its importance for subsequent steps, while more complex tasks like building the export feature or verification have higher estimates reflecting their complexity and critical nature.

rows.challenge: Coverage + ordering: schema change, three consumers, and a downstream job. Tests whether the plan notices the accounting export at all.

single.epic_title: Enable multi-currency checkout and financial processing

issues.title: Define supported currencies and conversion rules
issues.description: Specify the supported ISO 4217 currencies, minor-unit precision, exchange-rate source, rate freshness, rounding behavior, and policy for refunds and recurring subscription charges. Document the rules as the contract that checkout, persistence, and exports will implement.
issues.estimate_rationale: The main uncertainty is agreeing on currency coverage, rate sourcing, and financial rounding behavior before implementation.

issues.title: Extend monetary persistence with currency metadata
issues.description: Update orders, refunds, and subscriptions so each stored monetary amount has an explicit ISO currency code while retaining integer minor-unit representation. Add validation and application-level invariants that prevent mismatched currencies between an order and its refunds or subscription charges.
issues.estimate_rationale: This spans three financial tables, model validation, and compatibility with existing payment and subscription flows.

issues.title: Migrate existing financial records to USD
issues.description: Backfill all existing order, refund, and subscription monetary records with USD and update schemas, indexes, constraints, and rollback handling for the new currency fields. Verify that migrated amounts are unchanged and that existing reads, writes, and reporting continue to work.
issues.estimate_rationale: The work involves production-safe data migration, compatibility handling, and verification across multiple tables.

issues.title: Add currency selection and localized checkout pricing
issues.description: Add a checkout currency selector for supported currencies and display item, tax, shipping, discount, and total amounts in the selected currency. Obtain conversion rates according to the defined policy, show the applicable currency to the customer, and pass the selected currency through payment creation.
issues.estimate_rationale: This crosses checkout UI, pricing calculations, exchange-rate integration, payment creation, and localized money formatting.

issues.title: Persist multi-currency orders, refunds, and subscriptions
issues.description: Update order creation, refund processing, and subscription creation/renewal flows to write and read currency-aware minor-unit amounts. Ensure refunds default to the original order currency and subscriptions retain their committed billing currency across future charges.
issues.estimate_rationale: Multiple transaction lifecycles must be updated while preserving payment-provider, refund, and recurring-billing behavior.

issues.title: Update accounting exports for multiple currencies
issues.description: Remove the single-USD assumption from the accounting export job and include currency code and correctly scaled minor-unit amounts for orders, refunds, and subscription transactions. Update export validation and downstream file or API mappings so multi-currency entries cannot be silently combined or misinterpreted as USD.
issues.estimate_rationale: The scope includes export transformations, schema or format compatibility, validation, and downstream integration checks.

issues.title: Verify end-to-end multi-currency financial behavior
issues.description: Add automated coverage for supported-currency checkout, conversion and rounding, persistence, refunds, subscription renewals, USD migration, and accounting exports. Include regression cases proving existing USD checkout and exports produce unchanged monetary values.
issues.estimate_rationale: Testing spans several services and financial flows, including migration and backward-compatibility scenarios.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: The plan covers all the key components of the proposal, including currency selection, storage changes, migrations, and export updates. It also includes verification which is crucial for a financial system change.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Each task or story in the plan addresses distinct aspects of implementing multi-currency support without overlap. The dependencies are logical and ensure that foundational work is done before more complex tasks are tackled.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies between issues make sense; for example, extending monetary persistence (task 2) logically depends on defining supported currencies (task 1), and updating accounting exports (task 6) requires the completion of tasks that implement multi-currency in other areas.
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: The point estimates appear to be proportionate to the complexity described for each task or story. The larger points assigned to stories involving user interface changes and complex flow updates (tasks 4 and 5) reflect their greater complexity and integration challenges.

issues.title: Define supported currencies and conversion rules
issues.description: Document the supported currency list, currency selection behavior, exchange-rate source, rate freshness requirements, and rounding rules for each currency. Use this policy as the contract for checkout, billing, persistence, and exports.

issues.title: Store currency with monetary records
issues.description: Extend orders, refunds, and subscriptions to persist an explicit ISO currency code alongside integer minor-unit amounts, and migrate all existing records as USD. Update models, database constraints, and data-access paths so currency cannot be silently omitted.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires coordinated schema, migration, model, and data-access changes across multiple monetary record types.

issues.title: Add currency-aware checkout pricing
issues.description: Let checkout determine the customer’s selected or assigned supported currency, calculate prices using the approved conversion policy, and display formatted amounts with the correct currency precision. Ensure order creation carries the selected currency and final charged minor-unit amount.
issues.estimate_rationale: Spans currency selection, conversion and formatting logic, checkout presentation, and order creation integration.

issues.title: Charge payments in the order currency
issues.description: Update payment-provider requests and result handling to use each order’s currency and minor-unit amount rather than a global USD assumption. Reject unsupported currencies or mismatched provider responses and retain the currency used for the completed transaction.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires payment-provider integration changes and validation of currency and amount consistency.

issues.title: Support refunds in the original currency
issues.description: Update refund creation and validation to use the order’s recorded currency, including partial refunds and remaining-balance checks in integer minor units. Display refund amounts with the correct currency and persist the refund currency for downstream consumers.
issues.estimate_rationale: Involves refund validation, integer minor-unit calculations, UI formatting, and persistence updates.

issues.title: Bill subscriptions in their original currency
issues.description: Carry the subscription currency through creation, renewal, invoice, and cancellation flows so recurring charges use the currency agreed at signup. Prevent renewal logic from falling back to USD and expose the currency on subscription billing records.
issues.estimate_rationale: Touches subscription lifecycle, renewal and invoice generation, payment charging, and billing-record persistence.

issues.title: Generate currency-aware accounting exports
issues.description: Update the accounting export job to emit currency codes and currency-specific minor-unit amounts for orders, refunds, and subscription transactions. Preserve historical USD export semantics, remove single-currency assumptions, and define handling for missing currency data.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires changes to export mappings and reconciliation behavior across several monetary transaction types.

issues.title: Validate multi-currency billing end to end
issues.description: Add automated coverage for currency selection, conversion and rounding, persistence, payment charging, partial refunds, subscription renewals, historical USD data, and accounting export reconciliation. Include currencies with different minor-unit precision and unsupported-currency cases.
issues.estimate_rationale: Covers broad cross-flow integration testing, including precision variants, legacy data, and failure cases.

issues.title: Integrate the approved exchange-rate source
issues.description: Implement the exchange-rate integration for the approved provider, including retrieving rates within the required freshness window and making them available to checkout and billing conversion flows. Define and handle unavailable, stale, invalid, or failed rate responses so conversions do not silently use unsafe values.
issues.estimate_rationale: Requires provider integration, freshness validation, rate availability handling, and reusable service wiring for conversion flows.

judgment.completeness_reasoning: The plan covers all aspects of multi-currency support as outlined in the proposal, including currency selection, storage, processing, and accounting exports. It also addresses conversion and rounding rules, which are crucial for maintaining accuracy.
judgment.non_redundancy_reasoning: Each issue is distinct and necessary to achieve the goals of the epic without unnecessary duplication or padding. The tasks and stories build upon each other logically and efficiently.
judgment.dependency_correctness_reasoning: Dependencies are clearly defined and logically structured, ensuring that foundational work (like defining supported currencies and conversion rules) is completed before dependent tasks (such as storing currency with monetary records).
judgment.estimate_reasonableness_reasoning: The estimates provided for each task and story appear proportionate to the complexity of the work described. For example, more complex stories like adding currency-aware checkout pricing are appropriately estimated higher (8 pts) compared to less complex tasks (5 pts). The unestimated policy definition is a reasonable choice given its foundational nature.
